main_text.p: fesu fuit. Post quæ apertius explicans & evolvens Appianus rationes has, ob quas commeatuum angustiâ jam laborare inciperent obsessi, ait, mare circum urbem Carthaginem importuosum & præruptum fuisse, & fluctus ob petras maximè turbidos, ut naves Romanæ quanquàm circumsisterent urbem, tamen nec continuâ serie nec densim ibidem stare possent, nec propius ad urbem fluitare ob Pænos in muris consistentes: atque idcirco dicit, ab equitum Pænorum prædesto foris agente, observatâ occasione vehementius è mari afflantis venti, amissas celeres naves pansis velis, quas consequi triremes non possent, cum paulo frumento in portu Carthaginis interdum fuisse delatas. Quibus deinde subjicit idem Appianus: Vbi id senfit Scipio, conatus est claudere os portus ad occidentem spectans, & non longè remotum a litore. Produxit igitur in mare longum aggerem ab ea lingua, quæ inter stagnum erat & mare, per altum recta versus os protendens, dejectis & constipatis saxis prægrandibus ne fluctibus cederent. Ejus aggeru latitudo xxiv pedum fuit in superficie, in fundo vero quadrupla. Id opus Pœni initio videbant contemnentes, ut tardè aut for-tasse nunquam absolvendum. Sed cum totus

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout, as the rules require. "fesu fuit." at the top looks italic, so it is marked as italic; this is a continuation from the previous page. "Vbi id senfit" is read as "senfit" with long s, as printed; the reading is clear. Faint marks in the left margin (an "a" near the middle of the text and a Greek-looking "π" lower down, near "for-tasse") could not be read with certainty and are not transcribed. Faint mirrored marks at the lower left ("abs", "vɡ") look like show-through from the other side and are left out. "aggeru" is printed as such and is kept.
